title: Cost & latency ledger + slice generator for per-route/model/customer breakdowns
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Problem: The Console needs a single, auditable ledger and slice generation service that produces per-route / per-model / per-customer cost and latency breakdowns for dashboards, billing reconciliation, and SLA analysis. Current signals are scattered across streaming traces, host-level GPU metrics, and periodic billing dumps which produce inconsistent views and expensive ad-hoc joins.

Goals:
- Produce a canonical time-partitioned ledger of compute and latency attribution with stable keys: route_id, model_variant, customer_id, timeframe (1m/1h/day).
- Support both approximate streaming aggregation (low-latency dashboard updates) and exact daily batch rollups for billing reconciliation.
- Attribute GPU compute cost using a deterministic allocator that reconciles GPU-time, batch size, and KV cache hits.
- Expose slice generation: arbitrary group-by slices (route+model, customer+region, route+plan) with precomputed metrics for fast Console queries and alerting.
- Maintain traceability to source events (trace_id, request_id, telemetry_offsets) for audits and debugging.

Design notes / decisions:
- Dataflow: ingest normalization -> enrichment (map request->route, model mapping table) -> streaming pre-aggregate (windowed tumbling 1m) -> append-only ledger topic (kafka) -> daily exact rollup job (Spark/Flink) writes final canonical tables in ClickHouse and parquet S3 for backups.
- Attribution strategy: use measured device_ms per batch as primary cost signal. For multi-tenant GPUs we charge by fraction of device_ms weighted by effective tokens generated and KV cache reuse factor. This reduces variance vs token-only cost.
- Latency computation: compute p50/p95/p99 on request end-to-end time measured at ingress, with optional kernel-level breakdown when available. Streaming p95 is approximate using t-digest; daily job recomputes exact quantiles for billing windows.
- Sampling and extrapolation: for very high-cardinality customers/slices we keep a reservoir sample with reservoir ids and provide extrapolated totals; all slices include sample metadata so Console can indicate confidence.
- Schema: ledger rows contain only primitives: partition_time, route_id, model_id, model_variant, customer_id, device_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, kv_cache_hits, request_count, t_digest_bytes, source_offsets. This matches existing dashboard queries and is intentionally narrow for efficient storage.
- Backfill & migration: build an idempotent backfill that can replay historical telemetry + billing records to populate ledger and reconcile against existing billing insights. Provide a reconciliation job that emits drift reports.

Trade-offs considered:
- Streaming-first vs batch-first: streaming gives fast dashboards but risks approximation drift. Chosen hybrid approach with streaming for near-real-time and batch for authoritative numbers.
- Attribution complexity: a simple token-based cost would be easier but leads to mispricing for long-context KV-cache heavy workloads. Device_ms weighting improves accuracy at cost of requiring GPU-time telemetry.

APIs and consumer surfaces:
- Internal reads: read-only SQL views in ClickHouse for Console with materialized slices (route/model/customer) for the UI.
- Exposed endpoints: /internal/analytics/ledger/query -> for ad-hoc slices (paginated) and /internal/analytics/ledger/summary -> FAQ style aggregated totals. Both behind RBAC and rate limits.
- Events & dashboards: Grafana dashboard 'ledger-health' and a daily 'reconciliation' report in DataStudio.

Operational concerns:
- SLOs: ledger ingestion availability 99.95% and daily reconciliation complete within 4 hours of day boundary.
- Cost: ClickHouse retention policy 90 days hot, 365 days cold (parquet).
- Monitoring: alerts for Kafka consumer lag > 5m, daily rollup failing, reconciliation drift > 0.5% for top-10 customers.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for allocator and t-digest aggregation.
- Integration tests that replay synthetic telemetry and validate ledger invariants (monotonic totals, idempotency).
- Load test: ingest 200k req/s equivalent in a perf cluster and validate latency < 200ms for streaming path.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy ledger write-only in staging; run parallel reconciliation against staging billing.
2) Canary ingest real traffic for low-volume customers (alpha list) with streaming metrics surfaced in beta dashboard.
3) Run daily batch reconciliation and validate drift < 0.2% for the canary customers for 7 days.
4) Gradual ramp to all customers, then switch Console to authoritative views from ledger.

Audit / compliance notes: ledger includes pointers to request-level traces but not full PII. Customer data access is gated and audited. KMS keys used for any encrypted fields.

updates: 2026-02-08: Initial spike completed — validated device_ms can be emitted from serving runtime with <1% overhead. Produced prototype allocator code and unit tests.
2026-02-15: Design review with PM and Observability team. Feedback: include sampling metadata and explicit confidence intervals on Console. Action: add reservoir sampling to streaming pre-agg.
2026-02-22: Blocked — missing stable model mapping service v2 (needed to map alias->model_variant). Dependency ticket ENG-19612 created; working with Model Infra to finalize API.
2026-02-28: Implementation started for streaming pre-agg (Flink). Basic windowed 1m tumblers emitting to ledger-kafka topic. Ingest tested in dev cluster at modest load.

2026-03-02: Performance testing scheduled. Identified potential cost increase if ClickHouse cardinality spikes; investigating pre-aggregation rollups and TTL tuning. Next: implement downsampling for low-impact slices.
